_comment: Edit this file, not the code. Bands: 1 cheap workhorse, 2 mid, 3 deep. Ladders are ordered preferences; the router filters by live quota and then prefers the eligible candidate whose quota bucket resets soonest (spend what expires first).
_comment_reserves: zai_coding_plan has no reserve because the GLM Coding Plan publishes no quota API: there is no reading to hold a reserve against, and the unmetered flag (not a number) is what policy gates on.

claude._note: Legacy fallback only when native get_usage control is unavailable. This is a declared allowance, not a measured subscription limit; transcript estimates remain labelled computed. Native subscription percentages take precedence. Lower the fallback budget to hold Claude back; null leaves fallback headroom unknown.

openrouter._note: 1000/day applies with 10 USD or more of lifetime credit, otherwise 50/day. Counted locally in state.json.

_comment_bands: Owner policy 2026-10-08: routine work defaults to MiniMax, then glm-5.3-flash. Difficult work is luna, terra, sol on the top band or a retry after luna and terra, sonnet-5-5, opus-5-5 only after sonnet failed, then nothing eligible. Claude remains above its 30% reserve and never serves routine work.
_comment_free: opencode_zen's -free models are still probed but are off every ladder. Measured 2026-09-20 (docs/FREE-MODELS.md): eight calls across two models and two coding tasks returned 0 usable answers, every one failing with 'Rate limit exceeded. Please try again later.' before any output. Their coding ability and their speed are therefore unmeasured, not slow: the old claim that they were slow came from timing a call that never produced an answer. Retest with `opencode run -m opencode/nemotron-3-ultra-free "reply with exactly: OK"` and put them back on band 1 if it answers.
_comment_cache: Seconds a quota reading stays usable for routing. A dispatch takes minutes, so a reading a minute old is the same reading. `rightsize probe` and `route --fresh` always re-read.

launchers._doc: How a decision becomes a command. Each launcher maps a provider to a template, with `default` covering the rest. Fields: {provider} {agent} {model} {model_ref} {effort} {band} {spec} {spec_path}. Adding a launcher is config, not code: see docs/ADAPTERS.md.

orca._doc: A worker-start launches a worker, which is by definition not the coordinator, so it gets its own worktree. `--worktree current` reuses the main checkout: the worker shares the coordinator's tree and branch, can write to main mid-merge, and cleanup can never find it because there is no worktree to remove. One such worker ran in a main checkout for 29 hours. For opencode the model is bound by creating the terminal with `opencode -m <model>` and attaching the worker to it, because `--agent opencode` takes no model flag and `OPENCODE_MODEL` is ignored: a worker launched without the binding silently runs the default in ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json, and `rightsize audit` exists to catch exactly that. The chosen effort is optionally written to a state file outside the worker worktree and loaded through OPENCODE_CONFIG; generic provider paths were wire-tested, but built-in coding-plan paths remain unverified. Evaluate OpenCode's native `-m provider/model#variant` form separately. Use orca-current only when sharing the checkout is the point.

orca-current._doc: Deliberately shares the coordinator's checkout. For a supervised leg you are watching, a quick review, or a task that must see uncommitted work in the current tree. Never for unsupervised work. For opencode, export OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT with the model options JSON from the route's launch line before starting `opencode -m <model_ref>`, so the chosen effort still reaches the model.
orca-current.default:
orca orchestration worker-start --spec {spec} --worktree current --agent {agent} --json
# then inside that terminal: env OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT='__RIGHTSIZE_MODEL_OPTIONS__' opencode -m {model_ref}

_comment_dispatch_cost_models: Owner policy 2026-10-08: premium GLM models are spent sparingly, so one dispatch on them is estimated at a higher base than the provider default (then multiplied by the band, and halved off-peak). Cheap GLM flash/turbo/4.7 stay at the provider base.
_comment_dispatch_cost: Percentage points one dispatch is expected to burn, multiplied by the band. A coarse estimate on purpose: the exact number is unknowable before the worker runs, and being roughly right is what stops a fan-out from overcommitting a plan. Raise it if a batch of workers routinely takes a provider past its reserve.
_comment_max_inflight: How many dispatches may be in flight on one provider at once. This is the spread lever for a large fan-out: when a provider is full the next task goes to the next eligible one instead of queueing behind it.
_comment_reservation: How long a reservation holds capacity when nobody reports the dispatch done. A worker that dies silently must not hold a plan hostage, so this expires on its own; `rightsize report <provider> --done` releases it immediately. A hold taken before the launch (plan --reserve, which prints commands someone may never run) uses the shorter unconfirmed clock, because the common way to create a phantom is to print a plan and not dispatch it. A hold taken after a launch has actually run keeps the full one.

effort._comment: Reasoning effort per band, for the CLIs that take the knob. The band picks the model; effort is the second dial on that model. A wide blast radius, an irreversible step, or a retry after a failed attempt each raise it one level. Providers absent here get no effort flag at all. Levels: low, medium, high, xhigh, max.

effort_options._doc: How a chosen effort level becomes OpenCode per-model options. Generic OpenAI-compatible and Anthropic provider paths were wire-tested on 2026-10-08; the built-in zai-coding-plan and minimax-coding-plan paths remain unverified. Evaluate OpenCode's native `-m provider/model#variant` form separately. MiniMax emits no effort options until its built-in path is verified. Models whose profile lists no efforts never emit options.

peak_windows._doc: Vendor pricing schedule for premium models, quoted from docs.z.ai/devpack/overview: 'During off-peak hours, model usage is charged at 50% of the standard credit rate' with 'Peak hours: Monday to Friday, 14:00-18:00 Singapore Standard Time (UTC+8)'. weekdays are Python weekday numbers with Monday=0. During peak (or an unresolvable timezone) premium models are not routed at all; off-peak their dispatch cost is multiplied by off_peak_multiplier.

_comment_openrouter: OpenRouter is probed but deliberately not on a worker ladder. Verified 2026-09-20: its free models answer a direct API call, but dispatching one through the opencode CLI fails with 413 Request too large, because an agent sends a system prompt and tool definitions that the free endpoint will not accept. Put it back on a ladder once either a paid model is laddered (the key here carries its own 0.01 USD spend limit, so raise that first at openrouter.ai/settings/keys) or a launcher exists that dispatches with a small payload.
_comment_staleness: How old a file-sourced reading may be before it is treated as unknown rather than current. Only Codex needs this: its numbers are written when Codex runs, so between sessions the reading ages while the real quota moves. An old HIGH reading is the dangerous direction, because it blocks a provider that may have reset hours ago, and unknown already means escalation-only rather than unusable. Verified 2026-09-20: `codex exec` does not write a rollout, so only an interactive Codex session refreshes this.
_comment_comfort: At or above this band, the pick prefers the plan with the most headroom instead of the bucket expiring soonest. Expiring capacity is worth more spent on cheap work, and the expensive rung usually has a roomier plan available: money.financial hit the opposite on 2026-09-20, putting a design task on an opencode weekly bucket with 8 points left and 19 hours to run while codex sat at 0 per cent with a week. Set it to 4 to disable.

minimax._note: Direct global Token Plan, separate from OpenCode Go. Uses MINIMAX_API_KEY or native minimax-coding-plan auth. Dispatch cost is an uncalibrated estimate; live rolling and weekly percentages remain authoritative.

zai_coding_plan._note: Z.AI GLM Coding Plan (Max) through OpenCode's zai-coding-plan auth. The plan meters 5-hour and weekly credits but publishes no quota API (checked 2026-10-08 across docs.z.ai, the OpenAPI spec, models.dev and Z.AI's coding-helper package), so the probe reports unmetered and the plan is offered behind the metered ones. What the plan can serve is recorded by refresh from the plan's own model list; the highspeed ids are refused by this subscription.

Claude is eligible only above its 30% reserve and never for routine work; haiku and Astra remain forbidden. Code-enforced candidate exclusion applies to every band, fallback, review role, route, plan and rerun. An empty eligible set blocks with no substitution, band descent or quality-floor relaxation.

_comment_profiles: Task capability assignments preserve the existing ladder as provisional policy, not measured superiority. Codex effort lists reflect the local native catalog on 2026-09-21; Claude uses a conservative configured subset. Empty effort lists mean no exposed runtime knob. min_task_band (optional) reserves a model for task classes whose task_profiles floor is at least that band, so deep-tier models stay out of routine work even when a routine task escalates bands. Profile every added model; quota never relaxes capabilities or task/retry floors.
